title: Lung and cardiovascular function trajectories of former very preterm infants from childhood to adulthood - a prospective observational follow-up study (PROSPECT study)
summary: The outcomes for premature infants with very low birth weight have improved but remain associated with lifelong risks. Lung function is particularly affected, with bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) being a key criterion. Future research should focus on long-term lung outcomes and various disease phenotypes. The Ulmer PROSPECT cohort study aims to investigate pulmonary outcomes and their connection to other factors. The results can enhance the treatment of premature infants and expand our understanding of long-term impacts.
conditions: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia originating in the perinatal period

interventions.name: All former preterm infants with very low birth weight (VLBW) born at the perinatal center in Ulm are offered a follow-up examination as part of clinical routine, which includes lung function testing and cardiovascular assessment twice, at the agesof 12years. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- VLBW infants born at the perinatal center Ulm at the age of 12 years
- Control group: healthy control subjects at the age of 12 years
Exclusion criteria:
- No parental or caregivers´ consent.
- Severe neurologic impairment that does not allow lung function and exercise capacity testing.
- Severe congenital malformation according to the international classification (excluding inguinal hernia, PDA, atrial septal defects, ventricular septal defects and all congenital anomalies that do not affect pulmonary, cardiovascular and psychomotor capacities).
